sections.heading: A Site-to-Site VPN joins your network to AWS through two IPsec tunnels

plan.problem: A data center must send files to a VPC this month over an encrypted link. The team has one router that can run IPsec.
trace: **Describe your side.** A customer gateway is [An AWS resource which provides information to AWS] about your router (site-to-site-vpn-concept-customer-gateway-is-aws-resource); creating it does [not configure or create the customer gateway device] (site-to-site-vpn-cgw-resource-does-not-configure-device).

**Pick the AWS side.** The target gateway is [a VPN endpoint for the Amazon side] (site-to-site-vpn-target-gateway-generic-term): a virtual private gateway, [a regional, highly redundant service] (site-to-site-vpn-vgw-regional-terminates-vpn-and-private-vifs), or a transit gateway.

**Build two tunnels.** Each connection has two tunnels, [each terminating in a different Availability Zone] (site-to-site-vpn-two-tunnels-different-availability-zones); each tunnel is [An encrypted link where data can pass] (site-to-site-vpn-concept-vpn-tunnel-encrypted-link).

**Bring them up.** By default the [customer gateway device must bring up the tunnels] (site-to-site-vpn-cgw-initiates-ike-by-default), and a pre-shared key is [the default authentication option] (site-to-site-vpn-psk-default-authentication).
plan.table_note: No table: the trace has one case. The virtual private gateway or transit gateway choice is the fast compare table 2.
plan.why: Why two tunnels? AWS [applies tunnel endpoint updates to one tunnel] at a time (site-to-site-vpn-endpoint-update-one-tunnel-at-a-time), so the other tunnel keeps the connection up while one is updated.
plan.exam_signal: "an encrypted connection between the data center and the VPC over the internet" points to Site-to-Site VPN, which supports [Internet Protocol security (IPsec) VPN connections] (site-to-site-vpn-definition-ipsec-vpc-to-on-premises); "the company must manage both ends of the VPN itself" points to a software VPN on Amazon EC2, where [you must manage the software appliance] (site-to-site-vpn-software-vpn-ec2-you-manage-appliance-single-point-of-failure).
plan.exam_trap_text: Wrong belief: one configured tunnel is enough, and the second is optional. Truth: AWS says to [configure both tunnels for redundancy] (site-to-site-vpn-two-tunnels-unique-public-ip-configure-both); during an endpoint replacement, [connectivity over the tunnel might be interrupted] (site-to-site-vpn-endpoint-replacement-interrupts-tunnel). End with <!-- trap: hybrid-networking-trap-one-tunnel-is-enough -->. At most 45 words.
plan.try_it: Try it callout for hybrid-networking-t02 after the Exam trap, ending with its task comment.
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: NAT, IKE and keys (at most 60 words). Behind NAT, AWS needs [the public IP address of your NAT device] (site-to-site-vpn-cgw-behind-nat-use-nat-public-ip); without NAT-T, disable it, or AWS tries [UDP port 4500] (site-to-site-vpn-nat-t-udp-4500-if-not-disabled). AWS can start IKE, [supported for IKEv2 only] (site-to-site-vpn-aws-initiated-ike-needs-cgw-public-ip-and-ikev2). You can [store pre-shared keys (PSKs) in AWS Secrets Manager] (site-to-site-vpn-psk-store-in-secrets-manager) or use [a private certificate from AWS Private Certificate Authority] (site-to-site-vpn-certificate-auth-private-ca).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: a Site-to-Site VPN is two IPsec tunnels over the internet. The thing to watch is that you configure both tunnels.
plan.stop_and_answer: A VPC already has a virtual private gateway for one partner's VPN. A second partner needs a VPN to the same VPC. Do you create a second virtual private gateway? Answer: no; a VPC takes [one virtual private gateway to a VPC] at a time (site-to-site-vpn-vgw-attaches-to-single-vpc); add a second VPN connection to it, which allows [10 Site-to-Site VPN connections] by default (site-to-site-vpn-quota-connections-per-vgw). Keep these facts out of the trace.

sections.heading: BGP moves traffic between tunnels and prefers Direct Connect routes over VPN routes

plan.problem: A VPC has a VPN and, later, a Direct Connect connection to the same data center. Both advertise the same network. Which path carries traffic, and what happens when a tunnel fails?
trace: **Choose the routing type.** If the device [supports Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), specify dynamic routing] (site-to-site-vpn-routing-bgp-if-device-supports-else-static); otherwise you [select static routing and enter the routes] (site-to-site-vpn-static-routes-device-without-bgp-enter-prefixes).
**Detect a dead tunnel.** BGP offers [robust liveness detection checks] (site-to-site-vpn-bgp-recommended-liveness-failover), so traffic moves to the second tunnel.

**Reach the subnets.** In the VPC route table you add a route with the virtual private gateway as target, or [enable route propagation for your route table] (site-to-site-vpn-vpc-route-table-route-to-vgw-and-propagation).

**Pick a path.** The VPC uses [the most specific route in your route table] (site-to-site-vpn-longest-prefix-match-most-specific-route); for the same prefix, the virtual private gateway uses the order in the table below.
plan.table: Same prefix on a virtual private gateway (columns: Order | Route source): 1 | [BGP propagated routes from an Direct Connect connection]; 2 | [Manually added static routes] of a VPN; 3 | [BGP propagated routes from a Site-to-Site VPN connection], where [the shortest AS PATH is preferred] (site-to-site-vpn-route-priority-shortest-as-path). Rows 1 to 3 link site-to-site-vpn-route-priority-dx-bgp-before-vpn-static-before-vpn-bgp (one display each; copy 'an Direct Connect' as AWS wrote it). Cells at most 15 words.
plan.why: Why does the VPN carry nothing while Direct Connect is up? The Direct Connect path [will always be preferred, when established] (direct-connect-vpn-same-vpc-failover-only-dx-path-preferred); on a transit gateway the VPN route is [which is the backup route] (site-to-site-vpn-tgw-prefers-dx-gateway-route-over-vpn) — write the sentence so that the display reads naturally, for example 'the VPN route stays hidden, [which is the backup route]'.

plan.say_it: The short answer is: BGP finds a dead tunnel, and Direct Connect routes win over VPN routes. The thing to watch is a static route that hides a propagated one.

sections.heading: Each VPN tunnel has a bandwidth limit and a transit gateway combines tunnels

plan.problem: Nightly transfers need several gigabits per second over a VPN. One tunnel is not enough, and the team wants no Direct Connect yet.
trace: **One tunnel.** A standard tunnel supports [up to 1.25 Gbps] (site-to-site-vpn-limit-bandwidth-standard-tunnel) and [up to 140,000] packets per second (site-to-site-vpn-limit-pps-standard-tunnel).
**One virtual private gateway.** On a virtual private gateway, [ECMP is not supported for Site-to-Site VPN connections] (site-to-site-vpn-ecmp-not-on-vgw-supported-on-tgw): it selects one tunnel.

**Many tunnels.** On a transit gateway, ECMP spreads traffic over several tunnels, and the connections [must be configured for dynamic routing] (site-to-site-vpn-ecmp-needs-dynamic-routing-not-static).

**Bigger tunnels.** A large bandwidth tunnel supports [up to 5 Gbps] (site-to-site-vpn-limit-bandwidth-large-tunnel), on [a transit gateway or to Cloud WAN] only (site-to-site-vpn-restriction-lbt-gateways).
plan.table_note: No table: the fast compare table 2 holds virtual private gateway against transit gateway. Use the words for the trace and the Why.
plan.why: Why does the transit gateway help? It adds equal paths instead of one: for example, ECMP across four large tunnels of two connections reaches [20 Gbps] (site-to-site-vpn-limit-ecmp-20-gbps-example). It also gives [an AWS-managed VPN endpoint] for many VPCs (site-to-site-vpn-tgw-vpn-many-vpcs-without-multiple-vpn-connections).
plan.exam_signal: "higher VPN throughput than one tunnel gives" points to a transit gateway: the VPN FAQ says to [use AWS Transit Gateway] (site-to-site-vpn-faq-tgw-for-higher-throughput); "more consistent VPN performance from a distant office" points to an accelerated VPN, which [uses AWS Global Accelerator to route traffic] (site-to-site-vpn-accelerated-uses-global-accelerator-nearest-edge).
plan.exam_trap_text: Wrong belief: more VPN connections on one virtual private gateway add bandwidth. Truth: together they are bound by an aggregate of [up to 1.25 Gbps] (site-to-site-vpn-faq-vgw-aggregate-throughput); move the connections to a transit gateway with BGP and ECMP. End with <!-- trap: hybrid-networking-trap-more-vpns-on-a-vgw-add-bandwidth -->. At most 40 words.
plan.go_deeper: Go deeper: accelerated VPN (at most 60 words). Virtual private gateways [do not support accelerated VPN connections] (site-to-site-vpn-accelerated-transit-gateway-only). [You cannot turn on or turn off acceleration] on an existing connection (site-to-site-vpn-accelerated-cannot-toggle-on-existing). You also pay for [two Global Accelerators per VPN connection] (site-to-site-vpn-pricing-accelerated-extra-charges), and with large bandwidth tunnels [Accelerated VPN is not supported] (site-to-site-vpn-restriction-lbt-no-accelerated).
plan.say_it: The short answer is: one tunnel limits the speed, and a transit gateway adds tunnels with ECMP. The thing to watch is static routing.
plan.stop_and_answer: A team moves four VPN connections to a transit gateway and turns on ECMP, but traffic still uses one tunnel. The connections use static routes. Why? Answer: on a transit gateway [ECMP is not supported using static routing] (site-to-site-vpn-tgw-vpn-ecmp-requires-dynamic-routing-whitepaper); recreate the connections with BGP. plan.problem: A bank wants its data to reach AWS on a line that avoids the internet, and to reach Amazon S3 and VPCs in two Regions over it.
trace: **Order a port.** A dedicated connection is a [physical Ethernet connection associated with a single customer] (direct-connect-dedicated-connection-physical-port-single-customer), at [1 Gbps, 10 Gbps, 100 Gbps, and 400 Gbps] (direct-connect-limit-dedicated-port-speeds); a partner [provisions on behalf of a customer] a hosted connection (direct-connect-hosted-connection-provisioned-by-partner).

**Reach the location.** AWS does not run your circuit: you use [local service providers used at your on-premises locations] (direct-connect-aws-is-not-first-or-last-mile-provider), and the [LOA-CFA is the authorization to connect to AWS] (direct-connect-loa-cfa-authorization-needed-for-cross-connect).

sections.heading: Direct Connect traffic is private but not encrypted unless you add encryption

plan.problem: A bank's auditor asks whether recordings are encrypted while they cross the Direct Connect line.
trace: **Private path.** Traffic [remains on the AWS global network backbone] (direct-connect-traffic-stays-on-aws-global-network-backbone).
**No encryption by default.** Direct Connect [does not encrypt your traffic] in transit by default (direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption).

**Add IPsec.** You can [establish a VPN over Direct Connect] (direct-connect-encrypt-private-connection-vpn-over-dx-or-macsec); a private IP VPN on a transit virtual interface does it [without the use of public IP addresses] (site-to-site-vpn-private-ip-vpn-ipsec-over-dx-no-public-ip).

**Or add MACsec.** MACsec gives [Layer 2 point-to-point encryption over the cross-connect to AWS] (direct-connect-macsec-layer2-over-cross-connect), on [10 Gbps, 100 Gbps, and 400 Gbps dedicated AWS Direct Connect connections] (direct-connect-macsec-supported-dedicated-10-100-400-gbps).

**Add a second location.** High resiliency uses [two single connections to multiple locations] (direct-connect-resiliency-high-two-connections-multiple-locations), for [an SLA of 99.9%] (direct-connect-resiliency-high-sla-99-9).

traps.belief: Direct Connect is a private line, so the traffic on it is encrypted.
traps.truth: Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic in transit by default; add an IPsec VPN over Direct Connect or MACsec, or use the transit encryption of each service.

traps.belief: A new Direct Connect connection can be ready within a few days when a deadline is close.
traps.truth: A new dedicated connection can take from several weeks to a few months; a VPN over the internet can be configured in minutes and bridges the gap.

traps.belief: Remote employees on laptops connect to AWS with Site-to-Site VPN connections.
traps.truth: Site-to-Site VPN connects an entire on-premises network to VPCs; AWS Client VPN securely connects remote users to VPCs.

traps.belief: One configured VPN tunnel is enough; the second tunnel is optional.
traps.truth: AWS says to configure both tunnels for redundancy; AWS updates tunnel endpoints one tunnel at a time, and a replacement can interrupt the tunnel.

traps.belief: With Direct Connect and a backup VPN to the same VPC, AS path prepending can send part of the traffic over the VPN while Direct Connect is up.
traps.truth: The Direct Connect path is always preferred when established, regardless of AS path prepending; the VPN is used only for failover.

traps.belief: Adding more Site-to-Site VPN connections to the same virtual private gateway adds bandwidth.
traps.truth: A virtual private gateway selects one tunnel and does not support ECMP; its VPN connections share an aggregate limit. A transit gateway with BGP and ECMP spreads traffic over many tunnels.

traps.belief: A link aggregation group of several connections at one Direct Connect location makes the connectivity highly resilient.
traps.truth: A LAG does not make connectivity more resilient: it does not protect against a device failure or maintenance where it ends. AWS recommends connections at multiple Direct Connect locations.

faq.question: Can two VPCs on the same Direct Connect gateway send traffic to each other through it?
faq.answer: No. For VPC to VPC traffic, [you must configure a VPC peering connection] (direct-connect-faq-dxgw-no-vpc-to-vpc-routing) or another VPC connection.
faq.quote: No, AWS Direct Connect gateway's only support routing traffic from AWS Direct Connect VIFs to VGW (associated with VPC).
faq.quote_note: Copy the AWS sentence exactly, 'gateway's' included. The second sentence of the evidence quote may be added if words allow.

faq.question: Can a virtual private gateway use Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN?
faq.answer: No. [Only Transit Gateway supports Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN] (site-to-site-vpn-faq-accelerated-transit-gateway-only).
faq.quote: Only Transit Gateway supports Accelerated Site-to-Site VPN.

faq.question: Can a server in the VPC start a connection to a Client VPN user's laptop?
faq.answer: No. [a resource cannot initiate any traffic or connection] toward the user's device (client-vpn-no-traffic-initiated-toward-client-device).
faq.quote: No, a resource cannot initiate any traffic or connection towards a user's device using Client VPN.

faq.question: Can Client VPN send only AWS traffic through the tunnel?
faq.answer: Yes, with split tunnel; other traffic is [routed via your local network interface] (client-vpn-faq-split-tunnel-routing).
faq.quote: If split tunnel is enabled, traffic destined for routes configured on the endpoint will be routed via the VPN tunnel. All other traffic will be routed via your local network interface.

faq.question: Can a Site-to-Site VPN back up a Direct Connect connection to an AWS Local Zone?
faq.answer: No. For a Local Zone, [you cannot use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN] as the backup (direct-connect-faq-local-zone-no-vpn-backup).
faq.quote: Unlike connectivity to a Region, you cannot use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a backup to your AWS Direct Connect connection to an AWS Local Zone.

Nightly transfers need several times the bandwidth of one tunnel. The company does not want Direct Connect yet. Which combination of steps meets the requirement? Five options. Never key on large bandwidth tunnels (volatile) and do not cite the VPN FAQ tunnel throughput facts (frequently-changing).

A company has a Site-to-Site VPN connection to a virtual private gateway. The customer gateway device has only one tunnel configured, with static routing. During AWS maintenance, connectivity stops for several minutes. The company wants the VPN to stay up during maintenance with minimal downtime and the fewest changes. Key: configure the second tunnel on the device and use dynamic routing with BGP (site-to-site-vpn-two-tunnels-unique-public-ip-configure-both, site-to-site-vpn-endpoint-update-one-tunnel-at-a-time, site-to-site-vpn-bgp-recommended-liveness-failover). (Select TWO.) An AWS Client VPN endpoint is associated with a subnet of a VPC, and users reach resources in that VPC. The VPC reaches an on-premises network, 172.16.0.0/16, through a Site-to-Site VPN. Keys: (1) add a route to 172.16.0.0/16 in the endpoint route table through the associated subnet and an authorization rule for 172.16.0.0/16 (client-vpn-other-networks-need-route-and-authorization-rule); (2) turn on split-tunnel on the endpoint (client-vpn-split-tunnel-default-off-all-traffic-through-tunnel, client-vpn-faq-split-tunnel-routing). Step 1: aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.99.0.0/16 with --tag-specifications for book=saa and task=hybrid-networking-t02 (capture VpcId). Step 2: aws ec2 create-customer-gateway --type ipsec.1 --public-ip 203.0.113.10 --bgp-asn 65000 with tags (capture CustomerGatewayId); explain: 203.0.113.10 is a documentation address and 65000 is in the private range [64,512–65,534] (site-to-site-vpn-cgw-asn-ranges-private-16-and-32-bit); the resource does [not configure or create the customer gateway device] (site-to-site-vpn-cgw-resource-does-not-configure-device). Step 3: aws ec2 create-vpn-gateway --type ipsec.1 with tags (capture the first VpnGatewayId) and aws ec2 attach-vpn-gateway to the VPC; aws ec2 describe-vpn-gateways shows AmazonSideAsn 64512 ([default ASN (64512)], site-to-site-vpn-vgw-amazon-side-asn-default-64512-not-changeable). speak.prompt: The bank says that Direct Connect is private. Does private mean encrypted?

plan.ten_second: No. Direct Connect keeps traffic off the internet, but it does not encrypt it. For encryption, add an IPsec VPN over it, or MACsec.
key_points_must: Private: the traffic bypasses the internet and stays on the AWS network (direct-connect-faq-bypasses-internet-dedicated-private, direct-connect-traffic-stays-on-aws-global-network-backbone).
IPsec VPN over Direct Connect encrypts end to end, with a smaller MTU (direct-connect-plus-vpn-tgw-ipsec-encrypted-over-dedicated-connection, direct-connect-vpn-over-dx-adds-encryption-reduces-mtu).

MACsec encrypts the link to the Direct Connect location, on 10, 100 and 400 Gbps dedicated connections (direct-connect-macsec-encrypts-to-direct-connect-location, direct-connect-macsec-supported-dedicated-10-100-400-gbps).
key_points_nice: MACsec is not a replacement for the encryption you already use (direct-connect-macsec-not-a-replacement-for-other-encryption).
must_not_say: error: 'Direct Connect is a private line, so it is encrypted.' correct: Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic in transit by default (direct-connect-not-encrypted-by-default-use-service-encryption).
error: 'MACsec encrypts all the way to the instance.' correct: MACsec is point-to-point on one Ethernet link (direct-connect-macsec-layer2-point-to-point-not-end-to-end).
follow_ups: Can we use MACsec on a hosted connection? No: MACsec is not supported on 1 Gbps dedicated connections or on any hosted connections (direct-connect-macsec-not-on-1gbps-or-hosted).
Do we need public IP addresses for a VPN over Direct Connect? Not with private IP VPN over a transit virtual interface (site-to-site-vpn-private-ip-vpn-ipsec-over-dx-no-public-ip).
plan.in_your_case: The recordings already use TLS on upload; for the link itself, a private IP VPN over the transit virtual interface encrypts the whole path to the transit gateway. Check-back question: 'Does the bank's questionnaire ask for encryption on the network link, or end to end to the application?'

speak.persona: a startup founder in office hours
speak.prompt: We need to connect our data center to AWS. Should we use a VPN or Direct Connect?

plan.ten_second: Start with a Site-to-Site VPN: it is ready in hours and encrypted. Add Direct Connect when you need consistent performance, and keep the VPN as backup.
key_points_must: A VPN uses IPsec over the internet and can be configured in minutes (direct-connect-faq-vpn-ipsec-over-internet-quick-low-bandwidth).

Internet performance is best effort; Direct Connect gives a more consistent experience (direct-connect-vs-vpn-internet-vpn-best-effort-low-cost-widely-available, direct-connect-private-connection-more-consistent-than-internet).
A new dedicated connection takes weeks to months (direct-connect-vs-vpn-time-dedicated-weeks-to-months).
With both, Direct Connect is preferred and the VPN takes over on failure (direct-connect-vpn-same-vpc-failover-only-dx-path-preferred).
must_not_say: error: 'Direct Connect is ready in a day or two.' correct: a new dedicated connection can take several weeks to a few months (direct-connect-vs-vpn-time-dedicated-weeks-to-months).

error: 'A VPN gives you the same steady performance as a private line.' correct: performance over the internet is best effort (direct-connect-vs-vpn-internet-vpn-best-effort-low-cost-widely-available).
follow_ups: Do we pay for Direct Connect when nothing is sent? Yes: port hours are charged even when no data passes (direct-connect-port-hours-charged-even-when-no-data).

Can we use a smaller line than 1 Gbps? Yes, a hosted connection from a Direct Connect Partner, from 50 Mbps (direct-connect-limit-hosted-port-speeds, direct-connect-hosted-connection-provisioned-by-partner).
plan.in_your_case: Check-back question: 'How much data do you move each day, and how soon must the link work?'
